message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom not to touch my flute. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, the flute is really important to me. It's not just any instrument; it's an Azumi Atlus, a professional model. I've taken great care of it, babying it, not letting anyone touch it, not even other experienced flute players. That shows how much I value it. I paid for it myself, even though my mom signed the contract because I was 17 at the time. I paid off $2,316 in 10 months on a 12-month plan, which is impressive. So, it's my flute, and I own it. Now, my mom helped me get it by signing the contract, but I paid for it entirely. She seems to think that because she helped, she can touch it whenever she wants. That's where the conflict arises. I told her no when she tried to bring it, and now she's calling and texting me, demanding to know where it is and saying she got it for me, so she can touch it whenever she wants. She thinks I'm being disrespectful. I need to consider a few things here. First, ownership. I paid for the flute, so it's mine. My mom helped with the legal aspect, but the financial responsibility was mine. That should give me the right to decide who touches it. Second, respect for boundaries. I've made it clear that I don't want anyone touching my flute, especially since it's delicate and expensive. My mom should respect that, just like I respect her boundaries in other areas. Third, communication. I told her firmly that she can't bring it, but she's not stopping. Maybe I need to communicate more calmly and explain why it's important to me. But she's not listening, which is frustrating. I also need to think about our relationship. We don't have a good relationship, and moving in with my boyfriend has made it a bit better, but not really. So, this might be another point of contention. Maybe she's taking it out on me because of other issues. On the other hand, she might feel that she contributed by signing the contract, so she has some claim. But I paid for it, so that should override her feelings. It's my property, and I have the right to set boundaries. I also wonder if there's a way to compromise. Maybe she can help me carry it or something, but not touch it herself. But I'm not sure if that's possible given how she's acting. In the end, I think it's right to stand my ground because it's my property, and I have the right to protect it. My mom should respect that, even if she doesn't understand why I'm so protective. It's about ownership and personal boundaries.
